Task: Classify CMIP6-based climate zones
Classify global climate zones for the year 2025 under the SSP5-8.5 scenario using NASA GDDP-CMIP6 data. It computes monthly mean surface air temperature (converted to °C), precipitation, and potential evapotranspiration (PET) using a simplified Thornthwaite-type expression. Task: Classify aridity and climate zones
Compute a high-resolution, discrete climate classification raster for the region south of 60°S using CHELSA v2.1 (1981–2010) bioclimatic variables. It derives aridity index (AI = annual P / annual PET), seasonal precipitation timing (HS ratio: Apr–Sep share), and thermal extremes (hottest/coldest monthly temperatures) to assign UNEP-aligned aridity classes (Humid to Arid Desert), then refines them with monsoon/Mediterranean seasonality rules and cold-climate overrides. Finally, it combines cold-class (100×), aridity/climate-class (10×), and summer-class (1×) into a three-digit composite code (e.g., 471, 672), maps those codes to a custom palette, and outputs a masked, visually styled raster layer exclusively for latitudes < −60°, intended for polar climate characterization.

Task: Estimate evaporation fraction from Landsat
Estimate Evaporative Fraction (EF) and related surface energy balance parameters using Landsat imagery. It computes the Ts-VI (Temperature–Vegetation) trajectory by analyzing the relationship between Fraction of Vegetation Cover (Fr) and Land Surface Temperature (LST), derives TVDI (Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index), models the available energy partitioning via alfa (decoupling coefficient), and calculates EF as a function of alfa, LST, and meteorological variables. Key outputs include Fr, LSTmin, LSTmax, TVDI, alfa, and EF rasters, along with intermediate layers such as LST and surface albedo, visualized using custom palettes.
